introH2: 🏝️ What kind of stays does Railay Beach in Krabi have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Railay is the corner of Krabi that's genuinely cut off from the chaos — there's no road in; you can only reach it by longtail boat, ringed by steep limestone cliffs and the white-sand beaches that are Krabi's signature image. It suits people who want to climb, kayak or just lie back and listen to the waves with no traffic noise · the upside is that the accommodation here is broader than many people think — from a legendary luxury resort spread across the headland to wooden bungalows and light-budget cottages that still get you a beachfront spot · a common problem is booking without knowing that Railay splits into two sides — the west is a pretty swimming beach, the east is the pier and mangroves — and picking the wrong side can leave you with an atmosphere that isn't what you had in mind · this article rounds up 8 Railay Beach stays we've reviewed in depth, working down from luxury resorts to light-budget bungalows — every one based on reading real guest reviews, giving both the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites with direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Railay has no road in; you can only reach it by longtail or speedboat — from Ao Nang it's about a 10–15 min longtail ride (landing on Railay West), or from Ao Nam Mao pier (landing on Railay East) · Railay West = white-sand swimming beach, the best sunset views · Railay East = the pier, mangroves, restaurants and bars · Phra Nang Beach = Phra Nang Cave, a famous climbing spot, one of the finest beaches in the world · you can walk across the peninsula between the two sides in 5–10 min · pack a bag that's easy to drag, since you sometimes have to wade through shallow water getting on and off the boat at low tide.

entries.name: Rayavadee
entries.revCount: Score 9.4 · 812 reviews · the legendary luxury resort of Railay
entries.badge: 👑 the number-one luxury resort on Railay · beaches on 3 sides
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Railay headland · Phra Nang Beach · longtail boat only
tags: 🍽️ The Grotto in a beachside cave
entries.addr: 214 Moo 2, Tambon Ao Nang, Mueang Krabi
entries.storyHtml: If you've ever seen the images of Railay's tall limestone cliffs and white-sand beaches and wanted to actually sleep inside that picture, Rayavadee is the stay that sits right at its heart · this 5-star luxury resort spreads across the Railay headland, ringed by beaches on three sides — Railay West, Railay East and Phra Nang — reached by longtail boat only · the rooms are two-storey Thai-style pavilions scattered through a tropical garden, and the highlight is The Grotto, a restaurant set in a rock cave beside Phra Nang Beach, scoring 9.4 from 812 reviews · the honest takes from real reviews are unanimous in praising the location, the service and the privacy · the honest caveats: it's the highest price on this list, starting in the five figures per night, and it's a big resort where getting around on foot takes a while.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: book well ahead in high season, since it fills fast · if you're on a honeymoon or a special celebration, try a Pool Pavilion for a private plunge pool · and reserve a dinner table at The Grotto in the cave beside Phra Nang Beach at least a night in advance.
pros: Railay headland location, ringed by beaches on three sides, rare and beautiful
Spacious Thai-style pavilions, highly private, set amid a tropical garden
The Grotto restaurant in a cave beside Phra Nang Beach is a memorable experience
Service and attention to detail score 9.4 from 812 reviews
cons: Highest price on the list, starting in the five figures per night
Big resort, a long walk around inside, reached by boat only

entries.name: Sand Sea Resort Railay

entries.storyHtml: Sand Sea Resort Railay sits right on Railay West Beach, the white-sand, clear-water beach that anyone coming to Railay wants to sleep closest to · it's about a 5 min walk across to the Railay East side with its pier and restaurants · this is a 3.5-star bungalow resort with several swimming pools, views of the limestone cliffs and the sunset over the Andaman, starting around ฿2,200/night with a score of 8.7 · the honest takes from real reviews praise the beachfront location and the value compared with other resorts on the main beach · it splits into a Sunrise Wing (the east side, lighter on price) and a Sunset Wing (the west side, closest to the sunset beach), so you can pick by budget · the honest caveats: some rooms in the cheaper wing are starting to age, and the beach out front gets fairly busy during the day since it's the main beach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you want the sunset view and to be closest to the beach, choose the Sunset Wing · if you're keeping it cheap, the Tropical Chalay in the Sunrise Wing is best value · and get down to the beach early before the tour boats arrive, while it's still quiet.
pros: Directly on Railay West Beach, the prettiest beach on the peninsula
The best value among the resorts on the main beach
Several swimming pools, sunset views, walk to Phra Nang Cave
Split into Sunrise/Sunset Wings, pick your side by budget
cons: Some rooms in the cheaper wing are starting to age
The beach out front is busy during the day since it's the main beach

entries.storyHtml: Railay Bay Resort & Spa is one of the few resorts that holds a wide stretch straddling the Railay peninsula — the front faces Railay West with its clear water and pretty sunsets, while the other side leads through to Railay East with its pier and restaurants · it's a 4-star resort with cottages and villas scattered through a tropical garden, 2 swimming pools including a beachside one, and an in-house spa, starting around ฿3,200/night · this is the stay with the most reviews on this list, at 3,752, scoring 8.5, proven by a large number of guests · it's an easy walk to Phra Nang Beach and the climbing spots · the honest caveats from the reviews: it's a big resort with rooms of many different models and ages, some cottages older than the newer ones, so ask for a renovated room when booking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: ask for a renovated room model when booking, since the cottages come in different ages · if you want a real sea view, move up to a Deluxe Ocean View · and make the most of the straddle-both-beaches location by watching the sunset on the west side then walking over for dinner on the east.
pros: Holds a stretch across both beaches, walk through to both Railay West and East
2 swimming pools including a beachside one, and an in-house spa

entries.storyHtml: Railay Princess Resort & Spa sits right in front of the Railay East pier, so you step off the longtail and drag your bag straight to the room — ideal for anyone who doesn't want to walk far with luggage · it's a 3-star beachfront resort of 126 rooms amid a tropical garden and limestone-cliff views, with 2 swimming pools including a rooftop pool that looks out at the cliffs, a spa, a kids' club and a fitness room, starting around ฿1,294/night with a score of 8.4 · it's about a 5 min walk across the peninsula to Railay West, the swimming beach · the honest takes from real reviews praise the value and the location by the pier · the honest caveats: Railay East is the mangrove side, not a swimming beach, and some of the lower-priced rooms have a musty smell, so move up to a Deluxe.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you're sensitive to smell, skip the Standard for the better-kept Deluxe · don't expect a swimming beach out front, since the east side is mangroves — walk across to the west instead · and head up to photograph the rooftop pool with its cliff view in the evening.

entries.storyHtml: Railay Village Resort & Spa makes you feel like you've dropped off the map from the moment you take the longtail in · it sits on Railay West Beach, which has no road in and is reached by boat only, a calm atmosphere amid the limestone cliffs and the sunset views the beach is known for · it's a 4-star boutique resort with 2 swimming pools in a tropical garden, spacious rooms of around 44 sqm with a balcony in every one, starting around ฿3,100/night with a score of 8.3 · the honest takes from real reviews praise the spacious rooms, the leafy garden and the beachfront location within walking distance of restaurants · the honest caveats: some of the buildings and rooms are starting to age, and prices rise fairly steeply in high season, so book early.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: choose Deluxe Pool Side if you want to step straight from the room down to the pool · if you're on a honeymoon, move up to a Jacuzzi Villa for the atmosphere · and stroll along the west beach for the sunset, the highlight of this side.

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about staying on Railay Beach, Krabi

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Railay Beach, do you have to take a boat?
faq.a: By boat only · Railay is a peninsula with no road in; you can only reach it by longtail or speedboat · from Ao Nang it's about a 10–15 min longtail ride, landing on Railay West · or from Ao Nam Mao pier, landing on Railay East · longtails usually wait until the boat is full before leaving, so pack a bag that's waterproof and easy to drag, since you sometimes have to wade through shallow water getting on and off at low tide

faq.q: ❓ Should I stay on the Railay West or East side?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style · Railay West is a white-sand swimming beach with the best sunset views, with stays like Sand Sea, Railay Village and Railay Bay (its front) on this side · Railay East is the pier, mangroves and plenty of restaurants and bars, usually lighter on price, with stays like Railay Princess, Sunrise Tropical, Railay Great View and Anyavee · you can walk across the peninsula between the two sides in 5–10 min, so choose the west if you want to swim right out front, and the east if you're focused on saving money and being near the restaurants

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time to visit Railay Beach?
faq.a: The time with the calmest seas and finest weather is high season, November–April, good for swimming, climbing and kayaking, but prices are high and rooms fill fast, so book ahead · during May–October (low season) there's more rain and stronger waves, and some boat services stop, but prices drop and there are fewer people · if you're coming specifically to climb, months when the sun isn't too fierce and there's little rain, like November–February, are just right

faq.q: ❓ Does Railay have light-budget stays, or is it only luxury resorts?
faq.a: It has both · the most luxurious is Rayavadee, starting in the five figures · but there are still light-budget options that get you onto Railay, like Anyavee Railay from ฿672 (the most basic, score 6.3), Railay Princess ฿1,294 and Railay Great View ฿1,400 · most of the light-budget group is on the Railay East side with plain rooms, but in exchange for a location you can't get anywhere else · choose by budget and check the real reviews before booking

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Railay stay · how do I compare 3 sites?
faq.a: Railay has a limited number of stays because the area is narrow and hard to reach, so it fills fast in high season · we recommend booking 1–2 months ahead for November–April and long weekends, especially Rayavadee and the resorts on the west beach · every stay on this list has direct booking links to compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com, since each site often has different prices and deals at different times · if your plans aren't fixed, lock in a free-cancellation rate first, then compare prices again closer to your travel date
